items.text: After an admin changes default_locale, stale fallback strings persist in cache until eviction because cache key doesn't account for SiteSetting.default_locale

Changing the site default locale at runtime could change fallback results, but TranslateAccelerator caches I18n.translate by config.locale only, which might keep serving cached fallback strings from the previous default locale until I18n.reload!/cache reset occurs
protect_from_forgery should be configured with 'with: :exception' to properly handle Cross-Site Request Forgery

The translate_accelerator.rb freedom patch has its own locale loading logic, and the new ensure_loaded! method adds another entry point that should be verified for race conditions or double-loading issues
'# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb' comment implies an ordering directive that nothing reads; ordering is purely alphabetical file-name sort

SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym is called without nil-safety guard, which will raise NoMethodError if default_locale is nil - should use safe navigation operator (SiteSetting.default_locale&.to_sym)
No test files are included in the diff for the new i18n fallback system

@loaded_locales tracking is sensitive to whether callers pass locales as strings vs symbols (e.g., 'en' vs :en), which can lead to duplicate entries and repeated loads - should normalize locale to a single type before checking/adding

New public I18n.ensure_loaded! duplicates load_locale's own already-loaded guard and its @loaded_locales ||= [] is inconsistent with translate which dereferences @loaded_locales unguarded (potential nil reference)
Use direct include instead of send(:include, ...) for I18n::Backend::Pluralization - Ruby 2.1+ makes include public on Module/Class
Use direct include instead of send(:include, ...) for I18n::Backend::Fallbacks - Ruby 2.1+ makes include public on Module/Class

Calling I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! in set_locale only makes fallbacks work for controller requests, but jobs/mailers that use I18n may not pass through set_locale and therefore may still not have fallback locales loaded

Cache key in translate method does not include SiteSetting.default_locale, causing stale cached translations when admin changes default_locale. The FallbackLocaleList#[] dynamically includes SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym in the fallback chain, but the cache key only includes the translation key, current locale, and backend object ID, with no cache invalidation when default_locale changes.

`@loaded_locales ||= []` is not protected by `LOAD_MUTEX`, introducing a race condition. Two threads could simultaneously see `nil`, each create a new array, and one write is lost. Consider removing the lazy init and relying on `load_locale` (which already guards access with `LOAD_MUTEX`) directly, or wrapping this in the mutex.
The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Fallbacks are now enabled in all environments including development and test (previously only production/profile/cloud66), hiding missing translations behind English text and possibly breaking specs that expect missing-translation output
No tests added for the new fallback order, FallbackLocaleList, I18n.ensure_loaded!, or fallback/cache interaction
Use of send(:include) to monkey-patch backend classes is fragile across gem upgrades

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The change adds no tests for FallbackLocaleList#[], FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!, the new public I18n.ensure_loaded!, or fallbacks behavior, breaching CONTRIBUTING.md step 3 requirement to include tests.
FallbackLocaleList class inherits from Hash but only implements [] and ensure_loaded!, meaning other Hash methods could return unexpected results if called by the i18n framework internally

I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is called only in ApplicationController#set_locale, so fallback locales are never loaded on non-request paths like Sidekiq jobs, I18n.with_locale callers, mailers, rake tasks and console. Keys missing in the current locale return 'translation missing' and that result gets frozen into the LRU cache.
FallbackLocaleList inherits Hash but only overrides []; fetch/keys/each/to_h return empty or raise, misrepresenting I18n.fallbacks since the Hash storage is never populated

The process-wide translation cache in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb keys only on key, locale, and backend object_id, but the fallback chain depends on per-site runtime-changeable SiteSetting.default_locale. In multisite, one site's fallback text can be served to another site, and after an admin changes default_locale, stale fallback stays cached until LRU eviction.
Process-wide translation LRU cache in I18n.translate is keyed only on key+locale+backend id, not including site; in multisite one site's fallback text is served to another site

`locale` is not normalized to a Symbol (or String) before the `include?` check. In Ruby `:en != "en"`, so passing a String when the locale was previously loaded as a Symbol (from `I18n.config.locale`) will bypass the guard and trigger a redundant load. Consider adding `locale = locale.to_sym` at the top of the method.

Fallback locales (site default, :en) are lazily loaded only via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! in ApplicationController#set_locale; Sidekiq jobs, mailers, I18n.with_locale callers and rake tasks never load them, causing fallback to silently yield 'translation missing' which the cache then pins
ensure_loaded! call happens on every request, which has performance implications
Preserve standard locale-ancestor fallbacks here; otherwise regional locales skip matching base-language translations.

issues.claim: The process-wide translation cache in I18n.translate (translate_accelerator.rb) is keyed only on the key, the locale and the backend object id. It does not include SiteSetting.default_locale or the site, even though FallbackLocaleList#[] puts the default locale in the fallback chain. As a result, stale fallback strings stay cached after an admin changes default_locale, and in multisite one site's fallback text is served to another site.

In ensure_loaded!, the lazy initialization `@loaded_locales ||= []` is not protected by LOAD_MUTEX. Concurrent threads read and write @loaded_locales without synchronization, which can cause lost writes or double loading.
The '# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb' comment implies an ordering directive, but nothing reads it; load order is purely the alphabetical sort of file names.
SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym is called without a nil guard, so it raises NoMethodError if default_locale is nil.
The PR adds no tests for the new i18n fallback system, including FallbackLocaleList#[], FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!, I18n.ensure_loaded!, the fallback order, and fallback/cache interaction.

Locales are not normalized to one type (Symbol or String) before the @loaded_locales include? check and insertion. Because :en != 'en', the same locale passed as a String and as a Symbol produces duplicate entries and redundant loads.

The new public I18n.ensure_loaded! duplicates load_locale's existing already-loaded guard. Its `@loaded_locales ||= []` is also inconsistent with translate, which dereferences @loaded_locales without a guard.
I18n::Backend::Pluralization is included via send(:include, ...) even though include is public since Ruby 2.1.
I18n::Backend::Fallbacks is included via send(:include, ...) even though include is public since Ruby 2.1.

I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is called only in ApplicationController#set_locale. Non-request paths (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, I18n.with_locale callers, rake tasks, console) therefore never load the fallback locales, so lookups yield 'translation missing' and the LRU cache stores that result.

Fallbacks are now enabled in all environments, including development and test, instead of only production/profile/cloud66. This hides missing translations behind English text and can break specs that expect missing-translation output.
Backend classes are monkey-patched via send(:include), which is fragile across gem upgrades.

FallbackLocaleList inherits from Hash but only implements [] and ensure_loaded!. Because the underlying Hash storage is never populated, other Hash methods (fetch, keys, each, to_h) return empty results or raise.
ensure_loaded! is called on every request in set_locale.
The custom fallback list drops the standard locale-ancestor fallbacks, so regional locales skip the matching base-language translations.
